what: Which of ICIJ's 968 World Bank and IFC projects are on this map, matched project by project. Checked independently in round 33.
method: Three passes, then the union, then an independent check.
Forward: 241 lead rows carry an r*_case_id written by a previous round; 3 more were matched inside the forward pass by P-number. That is the '244' the first method reported.
Reverse: every P-number the map prints was looked up in the Bank projects API and matched to a lead row with the same board approval date. It added 2 rows and both were wrong (see corrections).

Check pass (round 33 checker): all 120 monthly windows of the Bank's projects API for 2004-2013 were fetched (5,798 board approvals). Every one of the 968 lead rows was resolved to a P-number on its own name, date and country: 940 of 968 resolved. The map's own P-numbers were re-extracted from the whole case record rather than five fields, which found 13 the first extraction missed. 233 of the first method's 246 rows are confirmed by a P-number printed on the matched case; 12 of the remaining 13 are confirmed by the project name and approval date written in the card's own text; 1 was wrong.

Every unmatched lead row was then scanned against every case in the same country for its approval date in prose or its project name, which found 4 rows that are on the map under cases printing no P-number.
6 rows share a date with a map project and agree on nothing else. 5 are different projects and are not counted. The 6th (lead 73, Kandadji) is the same project and is counted.
what_this_is_not: Not the panel's 309. The panel counts map cases whose start year is 2004-2013 and whose lender list carries wb or ifc. 234 of those 309 match an ICIJ row; 75 do not, being Bank or IFC cases ICIJ never listed. And 15 matched cases fall outside the 309, because a case's start year is the year the harm began and ICIJ's year is the year the board approved the money.

Not a claim that the harm ICIJ recorded is on the map. 1 of the 249 rows (lead 276, Sao Paulo Metro Line 5) was dropped by a previous round after reading its documents, and is counted only because the map cites that project's appraisal and completion reports inside a case about Line 4.

Not a complete match. The method can only see a project the map names, by P-number or by a name close to the Bank's. 233 of the 249 rows rest on a P-number printed on the matched case; 16 rest on the project name and approval date in the card's prose.

corrections.why: Two Haiti projects were approved on 27 September 2012. ICIJ's row resolves at name similarity 1.00 to P127203, Rebuilding Energy Infrastructure and Access. The case rests on P120895 and its additional financing P130749, AF Infrastructure & Institutions Emergency Recovery, which is a different operation; P127203 is nowhere on the case. The parent, P120895, is already matched as lead 247. Round 32 had also dropped this row on its own completion report, which says at paragraph 96 that the project required no physical or economic displacement.

The case is about P117652, Central African Backbone APL2 in Sao Tome and Principe, approved 20 January 2011, which is already matched as lead 356. P108368 is APL1A in Cameroon, Chad and the Central African Republic. It appears on the case only inside the filename of one Evaluation Group assessment report covering four project numbers (126034-PPAR-P108368-P117652-P165413-P165415). The name similarity of 1.00 compared the Bank's name for P108368 with ICIJ's name for the same project, which tests nothing about the case. This was the only match in the possible-displacement table.

The card reads: 'IDA Credit 4277-KE for the Natural Resource Management Project (NRMP), approved 27 March 2007. The project funded the Kenya Forest Service, the agency that carried out the evictions.' The Bank's record for P095050 gives the same name, the same date and Kenya. The row was missed because the case prints P095050 only in an Inspection Panel case title, which the first P-number extraction did not read.

corrections.icij_project: BR Municipal APL: Teresina Enhancing Municipal Governance and Quality of Life Project
corrections.why: The card rests on the phase 2 loan of 24 February 2016 'after a first-phase loan that resettled 466 families'. The first phase is P088966, which the Bank's record gives under ICIJ's exact name with ICIJ's exact approval date.

The card reads: 'Lignite Power Technical Assistance Project (US$8.5 million, 2006-2012) paid for the mining Resettlement Policy Framework and the Shala resettlement plan.' The Bank's record for P097635 gives the same name and ICIJ's approval date of 12 October 2006.

corrections.icij_project: Ethiopia Protection of Basic Services Program Phase II Project
corrections.why: The card's conditions field quotes the 'World Bank, Project Appraisal Document, Ethiopia Second Phase of the Protection of Basic Services Project, 2009', which is P103022, ICIJ's row, with the same name and date. Lead 595, the Phase III project of 25 September 2012, is also added below.

corrections.icij_project: Ethiopia Promoting Basic Services Program Phase III Project
corrections.why: The card's lender role reads 'Phases approved 22 February 2011 and 25 September 2012', and the case carries Inspection Panel case 82, 'Protection of Basic Services Program Phase II Additional Financing and Promoting Basic Services Phase III Project'. P128891 is that project, same name, same date.

The first file lists lead 73 (Kandadji, P130174) among 6 rows that 'share a date with a map project and agree on nothing else' and are 'NOT counted'. It is in fact the same project and it is counted: round 18's own note records that the Bank titles P130174 'Kandadji Project' and gives the board approval date ICIJ prints. The score was 0 because the Bank files the project under the country 'Western and Central Africa'.

The first file says 11 annotated rows have no ICIJ row sharing that date 'because ICIJ printed a date that differs from the Bank's board approval date'. That is true of 1 of the 11 (lead 95, MDTF KP Emergency Roads Recovery: the Bank's record says 16 July 2011, ICIJ prints 7 July 2011). The other 10 were invisible to the reverse pass for a different reason: the map case prints no P-number at all. All 11 were checked by hand and all 11 are sound.

P103063 is printed on bisri-dam, but only inside the titles of Inspection Panel cases 127 and 134, which the Panel registered against the Water Supply Augmentation Project and the Greater Beirut project together. The case's own lender role names only the Water Supply Augmentation Project, P125184, approved 30 September 2014 and outside ICIJ's decade. Not counted. A person should rule on it.

corrections.icij_project: Rwanda Land; husbandry water harvesting and hillside irrigation
corrections.why: The name is the case's own project family, but ICIJ's row is P124785, a separate operation the card does not name; the card names P114931, approved 22 December 2009, and the additional financing Credit 5360-RW, which is P147543 of 19 December 2013. Not counted, on the same rule that left out Liuzhou Phase II, Liaoning Second and Third Medium Cities, the first Lagos Urban Transport Project and the Niger Basin APL-1.
